name: position_mapping
description: Learn how position mapping works in the Hermes Brain vault — folder depth, parent MOCs, link counts, and orphan detection.

position_mapping.summary: Position mapping organizes vault notes by their location in the folder hierarchy, nearest parent MOC, incoming/outgoing wikilink counts, and orphan status. Hub notes have 10+ links, connectors have 3-9, leaves have 1-2, and orphans have none.

questions.question: What makes a note a "hub" in position mapping?
questions.answer: A hub note has 10 or more total links (incoming + outgoing).
questions.hint: Think about the link count threshold.

questions.question: What is an orphaned note?
questions.answer: A note with no links in or out and no parent frontmatter.
questions.hint: It's disconnected from the rest of the vault.

questions.question: How does position mapping help vault navigation?
questions.answer: It shows which notes are central (hubs), which are peripheral (leaves), and which are disconnected (orphans), helping you reorganize and maintain the vault.
questions.hint: Think about hub, connector, leaf, and orphan tiers.
